item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ Open for critique
- Behold!

Preface: I am not a trans person, my critique is not going to be about the potential sensitivity of the article as I am not a good source to judge how it will affect trans people.

My opinion on this right now is that it's somewhat hollow as well as overlong. There is some horror imagery here, specifically:

When SCP-XXXX-2’s head has become engulfed, direct respiration, as well as the direct consumption of food and drink, becomes impossible. SCP-XXXX will provide SCP-XXXX-2 with an intravenous supply of oxygen, nutrition, and hydration, however the amounts supplied are suboptimal for survival.

and

This sheath grows from the attachment site at the back of the neck, over the head, and eventually covers the entire body. SCP-XXXX’s underdeveloped eye and mouth structures move to the front of SCP-XXXX-2’s head and become enlarged. Upon completion of this process, SCP-XXXX is considered to have entered its adult phase.

I do like the ending, but yet it feels hollow at the same time. I believe this is because the entirety of this article is a cold description of the anomaly and what it does. Not that these types of descriptions don't work, more that it's the issue at hand should be explored on a more personal level. If I'm reading this correctly, SCP-XXXX is the embodiment of transphobia, dysphoria, and self-hate. A cold, clinical description doesn't really convey that in a meaningful way.

My advice is to cut everything after the bulleted list and have the article pivot to either interview logs with an SCP-XXXX-2 instance. These would serve to show how SCP-XXXX functions on -2 while also providing the audience with a connection to this character. The ending you also have would have a bit more punch to it if we see these Foundation doctors supporting this character and their gender identity

cybersqyd recommended reaching out to more reviewers and I have to agree with ver on that.

Good luck!

item.title: Executioner From The Wild West: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Hey CogWheel1950: two things.

First: please don't reply to yourself like this; if you want to add additional context etc., please edit it into the original post instead of making a new comment.

Secondly: per the Draft Forum's policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies, authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor?

The problem here is that making it land better feels like it's…a lot more likely to feel jarring? Really though, my issue is more that the ending feels…not climactic enough? And I'm not sure how to make this feel more climactic tbh without leaning more into the darkness. This said: it might just be my natural inclination towards darker writing that's coming through here rather than an objective truth.

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

Like, I get this and accept your reasoning for this but it feels, to me, a little too loose and up in the air without the propagation; but at the end of the day, this is your call.

I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

It'd work better if there was some additional connection here; where like, -1 is the only one who can affect which way -2 goes but it feels…too much like that'd be putting everything on one person when really it's everyone that affects stuff. Honestly, I don't think it really adds much and I'd just trim it completely if you're not going to e.g. tie it into the end cycle or something instead.

item.title: Draft: The Holly King: Re: Draft: The Holly King
item.content:encoded:
Thanks a ton for taking your time to read through!

In all honesty I did not intend for his identity to be a mystery. Quit the opposite in fact (what with the image, and his anomalous abilities, by the discovery log I would hope people have put it together so that they understand the Interview conversation). I have heard that something is missing several times now though. To remedy this my idea would be to include how event the current containment procedures are not enough. A note explaining that no matter how much reprimanding or punishment they deal out, junior personnel are going to keep saying "we have santa claus in containment", in the same vein as how its joked that big foot is an SCP. This will, obviously, eventually cause problems. But, I may also replace that with something else.

Again, thanks!

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Follow up questions
wow you opened the box

but it feels…like the ending just kinda…happens?

It's important to me for multiple reasons that whatever other changes are made, The nature of the final paragraph remains. I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor? I don't want readers to gloss over it by taking it too literally.

it feels, like you'd have this great opportunity for like…the SCP-XXXX instance to crumble into dust and emit more parasites

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

like, the -1 instances really like…come together to crow about how good a job they did protecting their kid from being trans and like, regretting that being trans killed their kid

This is a good idea, but I can't think of a way to do it that isn't too heavy handed or takes away focus from the ending. Further advice would be appreciated.

I'm also kinda iffy about this starting in the mother at all as a thing; it feels…underutilised?

This is very fair. Originally the piece was going to be all about mothers, but as the scope of the metaphor expanded it fell by the wayside. I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

I…am hesitant only in that this feels…miserable?

I am very interested to hear some thoughts about how I could intensify the glimmers of hope that I want to end the piece with.

Thanks for some great crit.

item.title: Draft: The Holly King: Re: Draft: The Holly King
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I am…somewhat torn on this as a whole. There's a lot of charm to it that I like, but it feels a touch unsatisfying as a whole, I think in part because the interview doesn't necessarily go very far and really just serves to convey more about what the SCP is: it feels like this is a whole thing built on the mystery of who the SCP is and in turn the reveal of them being santa, and unfortunately I was lurking in #thecritters when grigori asked about that so I figured it out pretty soon.

I think it works as a whole though, and I would likely upvote this but?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

No other measures are necessary to successfully and safely contain him in his current state

I'm not necessarily sure that 'successfully' and 'safely' are both necessary here; safely contain to me implies successful but?

SCP-XXX is considered a nomenclative hazard (Eshu Class).

Something like "SCP-XXXX is an Eshu Class nomenclative hazard" might read better here; even if this is the phrasing SCP-4000 uses to refer to it.

However, previous attempts to contain SCP-XXXX per protocol 4000-Eshu have been deemed inadequate.

My personal preference would be for this to continue with e.g. "due to [reason]", namely, where the reasons it's been deemed inadequate are in some way shown.

I'd also lean towards capitalising protocol here and in the next sentence but it's largely a stylistic thing so w/e.

As an additional measure, the entrance of cell B5 is to be reinforced with iron.

I'd lean towards including this as a paragraph on it's own? It feels like it doesn't quite flow from the previous stuff but?

These alterations have been marked for differentiation from the standard formatting.

My personal preference here would be to explicitly say 'marked in blue' over making it blue, though I think it's clear enough without?

SCP-XXXX has knowledge of the name, middle name (if any), and surnames of all people it comes into contact with.

I feel like '…knowledge of the full name of all…' would be clearer, with like, middle/surnames being possibly mentioned in a footnote; though that feels unnecessary.

access granted

I'd probably capitalise this (Access Granted).

SCP-XXX was discovered during a performance of the 4000-Halloway procedure.

Minor note but this placeholder has only 3 X's so I'd probably add an extra just to ensure you don't miss it when changing the placeholder into a number.

which resulted in the appearance of SCP-XXXX in the chimney rather than an entrance to the the place of the nameless oddities.

this phrasing is a little ambiguous as to whether you mean "SCP-XXXX should have appeared in the entrance to the place of the nameless oddities but instead appeared in the chimney" or (more likely) "the entrance to the place of the nameless oddities should have appeared but instead SCP-XXXX appeared in the chimney"

This is believed to be due to the cultural association toof the epithet in question.

The following is an interview conducted on June 20th 1996.

This date is meaningless to us because we don't know when it is in relation to the discovery of the SCP: it could be two days later, it could be two hundred years later or it could be thirty days before.

however two members of security personnel were present beside the chamber entrance for emergency assistance

SCP-XXXX, I actually came to ask you a few questions. We want to know how you differ from the others like you.

Addressing the SCP directly here like this feels a little odd: like, there's only two people in the room, so it seems unnecessary for her to do this?

I see now, I see, you mean ██████.

See, this feels like it's hiding 'Santa' but it's a letter too long for that so I'm not sure if I'm wrong or this is a mistake?

Well, this clearly isn't the case for you, SCP-XXXX.

But, one makes duedo if they areone is to survive.

they to one here to keep the pronoun consistent

SCP-XXXX laughs

SCP-XXXX: I don't believe I ever said such a thing

Okay so this visually appears like it has an extra line but reading the page source, it's that none of the others do properly, probably because one of your ">"'s doesn't have a space after it?

(It's generally easier to wrap long things like this between "[[div class="blockquote"]]" and "[[/div]]", since it doesn't have awkward stuff like this)

Footnote 5. holly

I'd capitalise holly here

[-] Line By Line
